payload.answer: [hard] The ledger is append-only: a fork is a NEW job plus new events that reference the origin job and the fork point. It never rewrites, truncates, or replays over existing history. [hard] The origin job is not disturbed in any way -- not its state, not its lease, not its branch, not its worktree. If forking requires mutating the origin, the design is wrong. [hard] The fork gets its own git worktree and its own branch; vibey already manages worktrees under .vibey/worktrees/<cycle>/, so follow that layout rather than a parallel one. [hard] Idempotent under replay, like every job. [hard] Provenance is not optional: the new job must record which job and which point it came from, or a forked run becomes untraceable in the ledger. [hard] 100% branch coverage, domain purity, Conventional Commits, feature branch into develop. [soft] Forking a job that never ran, or one already succeeded, should fail with a clear message rather than producing an empty fork.
